request.spec:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A change that alters any person's overdue-total is now also followed by the rollup lines, and
every ROLLUP line gains overdue-total=<overdue-total> at its end, every TOTALS line
overdue-total=<total> at its end (a TOTALS line is written when any of its three totals moved).
A change of the sheet's today that puts a claim past its due-by, or takes one out of overdue, is
such a change even when no due or due-total moved.

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Overdue-totals are now in the rollup audit lines, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

The whole change is in `src/main/java/net/officefloor/hq/app/rollup/RollupService.java`:

- **Overdue-total per person:** it adds up the dues of that person's open or pending claims whose due-by is before the sheet's today. It counts the same claims as the due-total and skips claims whose due is n/a. It is not held to the sheet's cap. This matches how the screen already works out `person-overdue-total`.
- **ROLLUP lines:** these now end with `overdue-total=<x>`. A person whose overdue-total changes now counts as moved, so their ROLLUP line is written even if their claimed and due-total stayed the same.
- **TOTALS lines:** these now end with `overdue-total=<sum>`, and a TOTALS line is written when any of the three totals changes.

The front end and the stored data needed no changes. Changing the sheet's today already took a before-and-after snapshot of the figures, so a new date that makes a claim overdue, or stops it being overdue, now writes ROLLUP and TOTALS lines without any extra code.
